# `silk/npm/ini`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Parse the ini text of an `.npmrc` file into keys and values, the way npm reads it.

## When to use
Use [`NpmIni.parse`](#NpmIni.impl.parse) to read one `.npmrc` file, or any other file in the ini dialect of npm's
`ini` package. Find a key with [`NpmIni.find`](#NpmIni.impl.find). To read npm's whole configuration, with
environment variables, scoped registries, credentials, and the user, project, and global files,
use `silk.npm.config` instead.

## Details
Each line is a comment, a `[section]` header, or a `key = value` assignment:

- A line whose first non-blank character is `;` or `#` is a comment. Blank lines are skipped.
- `[name]` at the start of a line opens a section. npm reads only the keys before the first
  header; find them with [`NpmIni.find`](#NpmIni.impl.find), and keys in a section with [`NpmIni.findIn`](#NpmIni.impl.findIn).
- `key = value` splits at the first `=`. A line without `=` sets the key to `true`. A line that
  starts with `=` is skipped.
- Keys and values are trimmed. A value in `"` quotes that is a valid JSON string is decoded as
  JSON. A value in `'` quotes loses the quotes, and is decoded as JSON if what is left is a JSON
  string. In an unquoted value, `;` or `#` starts a comment, and `\;`, `\#`, and `\\` stand for
  `;`, `#`, and `\`.
- After that, the text `true`, `false`, or `null` becomes a boolean or a null.
- A key that ends with `[]` is a list. Each assignment adds one item.
- When a key is assigned again, the last value wins, and the entry keeps the place of the first.
- The key and section `__proto__` are ignored, as npm ignores them.

The input is read as UTF-8, and each invalid sequence becomes U+FFFD. A byte order mark stays,
as it does in npm: it is trimmed from a key, but a `[section]` header right after it is read as
a key.

## Errors
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the entries. Parsing has no other error:
  like npm, it skips the lines it cannot read.

## Gotchas
The text of a value is not checked against npm's types: `2` stays the text `2`. Dots in a
section name are kept. npm does not nest sections in its configuration.

## Examples
### Read a token and a list
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.npm.ini { NpmEntry, NpmIni, NpmScalar }
import silk.collections.list { List }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let source = b"//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken = abc ; a comment\nca[] = one\nca[] = two\n"
  let entries = run NpmIni.parse(source) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let token = NpmIni.text(&entries, "//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken") |> Option<string>.unwrapOr("")
  let count = match NpmIni.find(&entries, "ca") {
    Option<&NpmEntry>.Some { value } => List<NpmScalar>.length(&value.values)
    Option<&NpmEntry>.None => 0
  }
  if token != "abc" || count != 2 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `NpmIni` with `import silk.npm.ini { NpmIni }`.

<a id="NpmIni"></a>

## `NpmIni`

```silk
pub struct NpmIni
```

Functions that parse the ini text of `.npmrc` files and find keys in the result.

### When to use

Use [`NpmIni.parse`](#NpmIni.impl.parse) to read one `.npmrc` file, and [`NpmIni.find`](#NpmIni.impl.find) or [`NpmIni.text`](#NpmIni.impl.text) to read a
key. Use `silk.npm.config` to read npm's whole configuration.

<a id="NpmIni.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub effect fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> List<NpmEntry>
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the entries of the ini text `bytes`, in the order of their first assignment.

#### Details

Each line is a comment (first non-blank character `;` or `#`), a `[section]` header at the
start of the line, or a `key = value` assignment split at the first `=`. A line without `=`
sets the key to `true`. Keys and values are trimmed. A value in `"` quotes that is a valid JSON
string is decoded as JSON. A value in `'` quotes loses the quotes, and is decoded as JSON if
what is left is a JSON string. In an unquoted value, `;` or `#` starts a comment, and `\;`,
`\#`, and `\\` stand for `;`, `#`, and `\`. The text `true`, `false`, or `null` then becomes a
boolean or a null. A key that ends with `[]` is a list, and each assignment adds one item. For
other keys the last assignment wins. The key and section `__proto__` are ignored.

The input is read as UTF-8, and each invalid sequence becomes U+FFFD. A byte order mark stays,
as it does in npm: it is trimmed from a key, but a `[section]` header right after it is read as
a key.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the entries. Lines that cannot be read
  are skipped, as npm skips them.

<a id="NpmIni.impl.find"></a>

### Associated function `find`

```silk
pub fn find<'a>(entries: &'a List<NpmEntry>, key: string) -> Option<&'a NpmEntry>
```

Returns the entry for `key` before the first `[section]` header, or `None` if there is no
such key.

#### Details

npm reads only these keys. `key` is the decoded key; for a list, leave out the `[]`. Keys
compare byte for byte, so case matters.

<a id="NpmIni.impl.findIn"></a>

### Associated function `findIn`

```silk
pub fn findIn<'a>(entries: &'a List<NpmEntry>, section: string, key: string) -> Option<
    &'a NpmEntry
  >
```

Returns the entry for `key` in the section `section`, or `None` if there is no such key.

#### Details

It finds only keys after a `[section]` header with the decoded name `section`. Use
[`NpmIni.find`](#NpmIni.impl.find) for keys before the first header. `key` is the decoded key; for a list, leave
out the `[]`. Names compare byte for byte, so case matters.

<a id="NpmIni.impl.text"></a>

### Associated function `text`

```silk
pub fn text<'a>(entries: &'a List<NpmEntry>, key: string) -> Option<string<'a>>
```

Returns the text of the first value of `key` before the first `[section]` header.

#### Details

Returns `None` if there is no such key, or if its first value is a boolean or a null. The text
borrows from `entries`.

<a id="NpmIni.impl.firstText"></a>

### Associated function `firstText`

```silk
pub fn firstText<'a>(entry: &'a NpmEntry) -> Option<string<'a>>
```

Returns the text of the first value of `entry`, or `None` if that value is a boolean or a
null. The text borrows from `entry`.
